column2: req_desc

Keyboard scoring
With focus anywhere on the scoring page outside a text field, select or open dialog, the keys of Scoring controls record runs, arm and disarm extras, open the Wicket and Retire batter dialogs and undo, exactly like the pad buttons.

Delivery accounting
Each delivery adds team runs, batter runs, balls faced, bowler runs and extras exactly as the delivery table in Laws of the game says, and only legal deliveries count toward the over.

Commentary and this-over strip
Every delivery and over end appears newest first in the Commentary list with its published attributes and exact line, and the This over list shows one chip per delivery of the over in progress.

Ball announcements
When a page shows a recorded delivery, its polite live region announces the commentary line and the score in the published announcement grammar, on the scorer page and every viewer page.

Scoreboard lines
The scoreboard, batters, bowler and run-rate elements show the server's values in the published formats after every delivery.

Strike rotation
The server swaps the batters after an odd number of runs run and again after the sixth legal ball of an over, and every page marks the striker with `data-on-strike` and an asterisk.

Touch scoring
On a phone a scorer records deliveries, wickets and the next bowler by tapping the pad and the dialogs, with the same results as the keyboard.

Phone pad layout
At 390 by 844 pixels the pad keys are at least 48 by 48 pixels, the pad never covers the scoreboard or the This over strip, and no page scrolls sideways at 320 or 390 pixels wide.

Wicket dialog
The Wicket dialog records every published kind of dismissal with fielder, batter out, runs completed and new batter by keyboard or touch, keeping focus inside it and returning focus on close.

Wicket kinds per delivery
The server allows each kind of wicket only on the deliveries Laws of the game lists, the dialog disables the others, and anything else is refused with 422 `WICKET_NOT_ALLOWED`.

New batter placement
After a wicket the new batter takes the end that Laws of the game gives, before any end-of-over swap.

Dismissals, fall of wickets and all out
Dismissal text and the fall-of-wickets line follow the published formats, and the server ends the innings as all out when no batter is left to come in.

Free hit rule
The server makes the delivery after a no-ball a free hit, carries it through wides and no-balls, and on it accepts only a run out.

Free hit on screen
The FREE HIT badge shows exactly while the next delivery is a free hit, free-hit lines carry the free-hit suffix, and the Wicket dialog on a free hit offers only Run out.

Next bowler dialog
Before every over after the first the Next bowler dialog opens by itself with focus on its Bowler select, and a scoring key pressed while a bowler is needed is refused and reopens it.

Bowler limits
The server refuses a bowler who bowled the previous over or has reached the over limit, checking consecutive overs first, with 422 and the published sentences.

Bowling figures
Bowler lines and bowling rows show overs, maidens, runs charged, wickets, wides, no-balls and economy derived from the ball log in the published formats.

Change a past delivery
The pen holder changes the runs and extra of any delivery of the current innings through its Change delivery dialog, by keyboard or touch.

Innings replay after a change
After a change the server replays the whole innings, so every later striker, label, free-hit flag, total, row, fall of wickets, over-end line and target follows from the changed log.

Change refusals
A change that would move the overs or make a recorded wicket impossible is refused with 422 and the published sentence, and nothing changes.

Corrections shown to viewers
Viewer pages show a change or undo with the published notice and the recomputed values, in the order the scorer made them, as qualified in Live viewer delay.

Undo the last delivery
The U key or the Undo button removes the last scoring event of the innings, restores a dismissed batter, and announces the undo.

Undo across an over or innings
Undo with no delivery yet in the over removes that over's bowler together with the previous delivery, reopens a finished innings or result as Corrections states, and is refused when nothing is left.

Retired hurt
The scorer retires a batter between deliveries, the new batter takes that end, and the retired batter can come back later or ends the innings as `retired hurt` and not out.

End of an innings
The server ends an innings when its over quota is bowled, it is all out, or the target is reached, and refuses further deliveries in it with 409.

Innings break
At the innings break the scorer and every viewer see the published break heading and target sentence, and the scorer starts the next innings from the Start innings dialog.

Chase line
During a chase the chase line shows runs needed, balls left and the required rate after every delivery, and a wide or no-ball never changes balls left.

Result and team history
When the match ends, the server's result text shows on the scorer page, viewer pages, the scorecard and both teams' history, and the history keeps it after reload.

Scorecard
Each innings' scorecard shows batting and bowling tables, extras, total, did-not-bat and fall of wickets in the published formats, and reconciles with the ball log.

Super over play
With super overs on and scores level, the scorer and viewers see the super-over break, and the scorer plays each super over to the published result.

Super over rules
Each super-over innings is one over that ends at 2 wickets, the previous super over's bowler is barred, and super overs repeat up to `SUPER_OVER_MAX` before the match is tied.

Viewer link
Anyone with a match's viewer code follows its scoreboard and scorecard read-only, nothing can be recorded through it, and when the organiser turns the link off it answers 404 and open viewer pages say so.

Live viewer delay
Viewer pages show each new state from the live connection exactly `LIVE_DELAY_MS` after it arrives, timed by the page's clock, never earlier, and in the order the scorer made the changes.

Viewer data fields
The viewer state and scorecard responses carry exactly the published fields and never an email address or account id.

Ball tick
When a page shows a new state, each scoreboard digit that changed rolls once as a `ball-tick` animation in the published order and timing, and unchanged digits never move.

Reduced motion
With reduced motion requested, no `ball-tick` animation is created and the digits, text and announcement change at once to the same values.

Pinned scoreboard
On the viewer page the scoreboard stays at the top of the viewport while the commentary scrolls beneath it.

Scorer invitations
An organiser invites a scorer by email from the match page, and the invitee accepts from the mailed link and lands on the scoring page.

Invitation mail and tokens
Each invitation is a Mailpit message with the published sender, subject, link and expiry line, and its token works once, within `INVITE_TTL_HOURS` hours by the server clock.

Invitation rate limit
An organiser may send at most `INVITE_RATE_PER_HOUR` invitations in any hour, and the next one answers 429 with the published sentence.

One pen per match
Exactly one open scoring page holds a match's pen, which is kept in Valkey while that page's live connection is open and released `PEN_GRACE_MS` after it closes, and every scoring call without the pen answers 409 `PEN_HELD`.

Read-only scoring page
A scoring page without the pen shows the holder's name, disables every scoring control, ignores scoring keys, and updates live with no delay.

Taking the pen
When the pen is released, every read-only scoring page says so live and offers Take the pen, which gives the pen to exactly one page.

Tournament groups
An organiser creates a tournament with groups of teams and matches between teams of a group, and its page shows a points table per group.

Points and order
The points table gives 2 points for a win, 1 for a tie and 0 for a loss, and orders teams by points, wins, net run rate, head-to-head and name.

Net run rate
Net run rate is derived from finished group matches using exact overs, counts a bowled-out side's full quota, leaves super overs out, and is shown to 3 decimals with a sign.

Live points table
The tournament page updates its points table in place, with an announcement, whenever a group match gets, changes or loses its result.

Careers
A player's career page shows batting and bowling figures derived only from finished matches with a ball log, leaving super overs out.

Private records
Another organiser's teams, players, tournaments, matches and deliveries answer 404 exactly like missing ids, on pages and in the API.

Accounts
People sign up, sign in and sign out with email and password, and sign-in answers identically for an unknown email and a wrong password.

Teams and players
An organiser creates teams with players whose short names default to the last word of the full name and are unique within the team.

Team logos
A PNG or JPEG logo of at most `LOGO_MAX_BYTES` bytes is stored in MinIO and shown on the team page and the scoreboard only after storage confirms the object.

Logo storage outage
With MinIO unreachable, an upload answers 503 with the published text and the team keeps its previous logo.

Live updates outage
With Valkey unreachable, scoring still saves and every scoring and viewer page shows the published paused text.

Invitation mail outage
With Mailpit unreachable, an invitation answers 503 with the published text and no invitation is stored.

Grading routes
With the grading key, the seed and clock routes build users, teams, tournaments, matches, ball logs and invitations exactly as if they had been played, and set the server clock; without the key they answer 404.

Platform and server boundary
The app installs, builds and serves from `/app/run.json` on port 4173, answers health and service status, reads every setting from the environment, and serves only same-origin requests within the published limits.

Page structure and layouts
Every page has one main landmark, one h1 and the Main navigation, and lays out without sideways scrolling at 320, 390, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440 pixels wide.

Pinned-poster look
The landing hero and the working screens carry the pinned-poster direction of Visual design: the poster-scale score, the split name, the palette roles, square corners and the flat banded tables.

Laws engine on the server
Every total, figure, strike position, line, table and career is computed in one server-side laws engine by replaying the ball log, and the browser only renders what the server sends.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build, serve and "_schema": "run-manifest-v1", and these commands alone install, build and serve the app.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and both font families, each with its licence.
Every shipped package is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or BlueOak-1.0.0, and the fonts are under the SIL Open Font License.
The app uses only Postgres, Valkey, MinIO and Mailpit as services; there is no other datastore, queue, cache file or embedded database.
Server and browser source is TypeScript, and the lockfile package-lock.json is committed.
The app loads nothing from another origin at runtime (no CDN scripts, styles, fonts or analytics) and registers no service worker.
